title: Logins fail with 'token not yet valid' on one server only
intro: Users are randomly logged out, and the API logs 'JWT token not yet valid (nbf)'. The load balancer spreads users across api-01 to api-04, and every error comes from api-03. Its code and config match the others.

steps.prompt: Compare the clocks across the api group with an ad-hoc date command.
steps.fake_output:
api-01 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
11:02:14
api-02 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
11:02:14
api-03 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
10:58:41
api-04 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
11:02:15
steps.hint: Run the same command everywhere and compare.

steps.prompt: api-03 is 3.5 minutes slow, so tokens issued 'now' by others look like they're from the future. Check its sync status.
steps.fake_output:
api-03 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
 System clock synchronized: no
              NTP service: active

steps.prompt: NTP is 'active' but not synchronized. Ask chrony what its sources look like on api-03.
steps.fake_output:
api-03 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
MS Name/IP address         Stratum Poll Reach LastRx Last sample
===============================================================================
^? ntp.internal.example.com      0  10     0     -     +0ns[   +0ns] +/-    0ns
steps.hint: Look at Reach: 0 means no replies at all.

steps.prompt: Reach 0: api-03 can't reach its time server. The others use the cloud time source 169.254.169.123. Check api-03's chrony config for which server it's told to use.
steps.fake_output:
api-03 | CHANGED | rc=0 >>
server ntp.internal.example.com iburst
steps.hint: chrony's sources are 'server' or 'pool' lines in /etc/chrony.conf.

steps.prompt: api-03 was built from an old image pointing at a decommissioned internal NTP server. Push the standard chrony role to api-03 with the playbook site.yml, tags 'chrony', limited to api-03.
steps.fake_output:
TASK [chrony : Deploy chrony.conf] ***
changed: [api-03]
RUNNING HANDLER [chrony : restart chronyd] ***
changed: [api-03]
PLAY RECAP ***
api-03 : ok=3 changed=2 failed=0

steps.prompt: 3.5 minutes would take chrony hours to slew away. Step the clock immediately on api-03.

resolution: api-03 was built from an older image whose chrony.conf pointed at an internal NTP server that has since been decommissioned. chronyd kept running (so 'NTP service: active' looked fine), but with Reach 0 it had nothing to sync to, and the clock drifted 3.5 minutes over a few weeks. JWTs carry 'nbf' (not before) and 'exp' (expires) claims, so a server whose clock is behind rejects fresh tokens as not yet valid, and only for users routed to that one host, which made it look random. The same drift breaks TLS certificate validation, Kerberos (5-minute tolerance), TOTP codes, and log timelines. Prevention: alert on 'clock not synchronized' and on offset (node_exporter's node_timex_offset_seconds), manage chrony.conf with configuration management so old images get corrected, and prefer the cloud's local time service.
